result: Reducing from 3 algorithms to 2 uniform algorithms (50/50) improves over the 3-arm uniform portfolio, but fails to outperform individual constituents or standalone MOEA/D.
conclusion: Reducing portfolio arms from 3 to 2 raises the baseline uniform quality by +0.014 to +0.016 HV by providing 1500 FE per algorithm instead of 1000 FE. However, equal 50/50 splitting still severely hurts MOEA/D compared to its standalone quality (0.9651), and even underperforms NSGA-II and SPEA2 standalone.
